title: Two-Stage Mesh Deep Learning for Automated Tooth Segmentation and Landmark Localization on 3D Intraoral Scans

sections.title: 研究问题
sections.text:
《Two-Stage Mesh Deep Learning for Automated Tooth Segmentation and Landmark Localization on 3D Intraoral Scans》：研究问题的原文依据。

【Abstract · abstract-1-1】Accurately segmenting teeth and identifying the corresponding anatomical landmarks on dental mesh models are essential in computer-aided orthodontic treatment.

evidence.text: Accurately segmenting teeth and identifying the corresponding anatomical landmarks on dental mesh models are essential in computer-aided orthodontic treatment.

sections.title: 研究方法
sections.text:

【Abstract · abstract-1-2】Manually performing these two tasks is time-consuming, tedious, and, more importantly, highly dependent on orthodontists' experiences due to the abnormality and large-scale variance of patients' teeth.

sections.title: 主要结果
sections.text:
《Two-Stage Mesh Deep Learning for Automated Tooth Segmentation and Landmark Localization on 3D Intraoral Scans》：结果的原文依据；数值与适用人群以引文为准。

【Abstract · abstract-1-6】Our TS-MDL first adopts an end-to-end iMeshSegNet method (i.e., a variant of the existing MeshSegNet with both improved accuracy and efficiency) to label each tooth on the downsampled scan.

【Abstract · abstract-1-10】In the second stage, PointNet-Reg achieved a mean absolute error (MAE) of 0.597±0.761 mm in distances between the prediction and ground truth for 66 landmarks, which is superior compared with other networks for landmark detection.

evidence.text: Our TS-MDL first adopts an end-to-end iMeshSegNet method (i.e., a variant of the existing MeshSegNet with both improved accuracy and efficiency) to label each tooth on the downsampled scan.

In the second stage, PointNet-Reg achieved a mean absolute error (MAE) of 0.597±0.761 mm in distances between the prediction and ground truth for 66 landmarks, which is superior compared with other networks for landmark detection.
